races.title: State Assembly, District 21
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Diane Papan
cands.bio: Attorney and Democrat who has represented California Assembly District 21 since December 2022. Earlier she sat on the San Mateo City Council (2015–2022) and served as its deputy mayor. She also ran the nonprofit John's Closet in Daly City and worked in private legal practice.

endorsements.text: For 2026, Ballotpedia lists the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions AFL-CIO, California Nurses Association, California Teachers Association, IUOE Local 3, California Environmental Voters and Equality California, among others.

cands.gaps: The Ballotpedia list of bills she sponsored was empty on the page we read, so we could not document specific legislation she authored. We found no statements or actions by her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth limits and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay and pensions, or school choice and teacher pay. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2022, 2024 or 2026. We found no documented controversies about her in the pages we had. Her campaign site text appears to date from her 2022 run, so her current positions may differ.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia and Wikipedia say she was born in Millbrae, California, and attended Capuchino High School in San Bruno; her campaign site says she was 'born and raised in San Mateo.'

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Attorney (UCLA B.A. 1985, UC Hastings J.D. 1988) with several firms and her own practice; executive director of the nonprofit John's Closet; San Mateo City Council member 2015–2022 and deputy mayor; California Assembly member since December 2022.
qual.why: She has prior legislative service in the Assembly, plus local elected office and a law career, which fits the high band for writing law and the state budget. Committee chair roles were not counted.
qual.label: She has prior legislative service in the Assembly, plus local elected office and a law career, which fits the high band for writing law and the state budget. Committee chair roles were not counted.

pro-life.evidence: On her 2022 campaign site she says she is fighting to protect reproductive freedom, 'the right to an abortion and access to contraceptives,' and backed Proposition 1 to put it in the State Constitution.

second-amendment.evidence: On her 2022 campaign site she says she stands for protecting California's ban on assault weapons and is working with Rep. Anna Eshoo and gun safety advocates to protect it from future U.S. Supreme Court rulings.

cands.name: Jabra J Muhawieh
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 21. Describes himself as a San Francisco business owner, enrolled agent and licensed tax professional, and real estate broker. Helps run his family's grocery and liquor business. Holds a bachelor's degree from Arizona State University. Has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements or voter-guide recommendations from Reform California and several voter guides. His survey also names the San Mateo County Republican Party.

cands.gaps: We could not find where he was born or raised, or when he came to California. We found no record of his work before his current businesses beyond his own survey answers. We found no documented actions or stated positions on data centers, development and growth, foreign or institutional ownership of homes and land, immigration or H-1B visas, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice. His campaign website pages we could read had only slogans and a volunteer sign-up page, with no detailed policy text.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Owns a tax preparation and planning firm, works as an enrolled agent and real estate broker, and helps operate a family grocery and liquor business in San Francisco. He has held no elected office.
qual.why: Business owner and manager with tax and real estate experience, which fits the middle band. He has no legislative service and no documented policy or budget career, so he scores in the middle rather than the high band. The work history is self-reported.
